missions.name: WISE 0855-0714
missions.summary: The coldest known brown dwarf, 7.4 light years away, creeps west by about 8 arcseconds a year and glows only at 4 to 5 microns, so SPHEREx sees it in its longest-wavelength detectors and not in the short ones.

missions.name: Epsilon Indi B
missions.summary: A pair of brown dwarfs 12 light years away that orbit the star Epsilon Indi A and sweep south-east by 4.7 arcseconds a year, bright and clean in SPHEREx's 1 to 1.65 micron detector.

missions.name: Barnard's Star
missions.summary: The fastest-moving star in the sky, a red dwarf 6 light years away that marches north by 10.4 arcseconds a year, so bright that its centre saturates SPHEREx's detector.

missions.name: RW Aurigae
missions.summary: A young T Tauri star 500 light years away, wrapped in a dusty disk that dims and brightens it; SPHEREx caught it about 0.37 magnitudes brighter in 2026 than in September 2025.

missions.name: R Draconis
missions.summary: A pulsating red giant (a Mira variable) 2,600 light years away that swells and fades on a roughly 246-day cycle; it is so bright that SPHEREx only measures it from the wings of its saturated image.
